newsitem.title: POLAND: NOMURA SAYS HOLD STOMIL, DEBICA.
newsitem.headline: NOMURA SAYS HOLD STOMIL, DEBICA.

text.p: Investors should hold shares of Polish tyremakers Stomil Olsztyn SA and TC Debica SA, as they have good long-term prospects but high unit operating costs should cap profits in 1996 and 1997, Nomura said in a report.
The Nomura Equity Research report dated September 26 said such costs must decrease, in part because domestic demand would not absorb the firms' plans to develop all-steel truck tyres.

"While we believe that this (unit operation cost reduction) is possible, it is unlikely to show through this year and perhaps not even next, with the result that earnings growth will continue to be restrained," the report said.
Stomil and Debica are majority-owned by Michelin and Goodyear respectively.

Nomura said the stronger zloty was keeping sales down while domestic passenger tyre price competition was hurting Debica and a slump in agricultural tyre demand in western Europe and the U.S. was hurting Stomil.

Nomura said it was therefore reducing earnings forecasts for both companies, seeing Stomil earning 43.3 million zlotys this year, 53.3 million next year and 78.9 million in 1998 after having netted 55.3 million zlotys last year.
Nomura said Debica would earn 42.1 million zlotys this year, 55 million next year and 75 million in 1998 after having netted 35.6 million zlotys last year.
In a December 5 report Nomura had predicted nets of 146.4 million zlotys and 240 million zlotys for Stomil this year and next and 97.6 million and 142.6 million for Debica.
"Nevertheless, we continue to believe that the long-term outlook for both Debica and Stomil Olsztyn is good and recommend that investors should hold the shares," Nomura said.
